title: The Endocrine System
intro: **Exocrine** glands have ducts (sweat, saliva). **Endocrine** glands are ductless — hormones go straight into blood and hunt a *target organ*. Compared with nerves: hormones are slower and last longer (growth, metabolism

cards.title: 1.1.1 The Pituitary Gland
body: The pituitary gland is a small, bean-shaped gland located in the lower part of the brain.
The pituitary gland is structurally and functionally divided into two major lobes.

cards.title: 1.1.2 The Thyroid Gland
body: The human thyroid gland is a butterfly-shaped gland, located at the base of the neck in front of the trachea (windpipe).
The thyroid gland is critical to the healthy development and maturation of vertebrates, and regulates metabolism.

cards.title: 1.1.3 The Parathyroid Glands
body: Parathyroid (para – meaning beside) glands are usually four small, flattened glands which are located behind the thyroid gland.
The parathyroid glands secrete a parathyroid hormone (PTH), or parathormone, that controls the concentration of calcium ions in the blood.

cards.title: Worked: tissue vs organ
cards.problem: Is cardiac muscle a tissue or an organ?

steps.text: Tissue = group of similar cells with a shared function.
Cardiac muscle is a tissue; the heart (muscle + connective + vessels) is an organ.

cards.title: 1.2 Malfunctioning of the Endocrine Glands
body: People with one form of the disease, diabetes mellitus, cannot produce insulin.
Occasionally, glands of the endocrine system are defective.

cards.title: Disorders of the endocrine glands
body: **Too little growth hormone** in childhood → dwarfism; **too much** → gigantism. **Lack of iodine** → goitre. **Too little insulin** (or cells not responding) → **diabetes mellitus

tips.text: Levels: cell → tissue → organ → system → organism.

questions.q: The protein secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas is known as ______
why: The textbook: in the islets of Langerhans, the alpha cells secrete glucagon and the beta cells secrete insulin.
Glycogen is a stored carbohydrate (not secreted); ATP is an energy molecule. Answer: A.

questions.q: Calcium level in the blood is regulated by the
why: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium; calcitonin from the thyroid gland lowers it. Answer: A.
Textbook p.7: Calcitonin is secreted when blood calcium level rises.
